html:
SMTO-TSK-0015 — This task was removed and can't be continued

GUID: 233817fb-ca17-463a-869d-b55ac0837fd4
Slug: task-retired
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The task you tried to continue or start has been removed, archived, or its conversation was deleted. SMTO can't pick it up again, so nothing new was started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the SMTO page and check the Conversations pane to see whether the conversation still exists. The task or its conversation may have been deleted in another tab, and the page hasn't caught up.
  2. If the old task was changing files, sending messages or using other systems, check those places to see what it already finished. A removed task may have done part of its work before it was removed, and repeating it could do things twice.
  3. Send a new message in an existing conversation, or select New chat, and ask for only the work that still needs doing. A removed task can't be revived, but a new task can pick up where things are now.

What success looks like

  • Your new task starts and appears in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't try to reuse an old link or saved request to bring the removed task back.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The task, conversation or run has been archived, removed, abandoned or purged, or its request binding no longer has a continuable task record, so it cannot be started or continued.

What this means

  • The task/conversation/run is archived, deleted or tombstoned, or a retained request binding no longer has a continuable task record. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • The task/conversation/run is archived, deleted or tombstoned, or a retained request binding no longer has a continuable task record.

How to diagnose it

  • Check retention and tombstone state before selecting a retained eligible task; do not resurrect an old execution identity.

How to fix it

  • The task lane is retired or the conversation was abandoned/purged, or the task is archived. Reload the conversation list and choose a task that is still retained, or submit fresh work in a new conversation. Before replacing it, verify any external effects the removed task may already have produced.
  • Open current conversation history and select a retained eligible task. Reconcile any external effects before requesting replacement work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Any new work uses a supported retained or fresh task while original effects remain accounted for.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
